_readme: WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (three sources, one answer per point):
1. BASE = IAA GIS 2023a (gis/sport.json). The only machine-readable source: points, route lines, status. It is never edited.
The IAA has not published a newer GIS; the newest official source is the printed sport chart (Oct 2025).
2. POINTS = the table on page 2 of the Oct 2025 sport chart (code, Hebrew name, type, coordinates).
Used ONLY where the GIS lacks a point or disagrees with the chart. The other 203 GIS points already match the table within 40 m and stay as they are.
3. ROUTES = the drawing on the Oct 2025 chart (which points are joined, solid or dotted, colour, printed distance).
The table has no routes, so legs come from the drawing. Sport legs are straight lines between their points.
The printed distance is a CHECK on the typed coordinates: the parser computes the leg length from the coordinates and
refuses the leg (Q circle + flag) if it differs from the printed distance by more than 0.3 NM (a typo in a coordinate).
NAMING: the chart's code is the official one. Older or other codes (GIS 2023a, CVFR chart, codes the NOTAMs use) are kept
as aliases, so a NOTAM written with any of them still finds the point.
STATUS words as in the GIS: OPEN = solid line; BR = dotted line = with controller approval only (chart legend: 'באישור בקר/פקח בלבד').
AllWeek = green, Weekend = brown, מיוחד = purple (as on the chart).
PRIORITY: where this file and the GIS both hold a point, this file wins. Drop this file when the IAA publishes a new GIS.
WITHDRAWN (not deleted): points / legs that are in the GIS but no longer on the 2025 chart. They are hidden wherever a pilot
plans or looks (map layers, route drawing, waypoint names), so no one plans along a route that no longer exists,
but the NOTAM parser still knows them: a NOTAM that names one is still DRAWN (hiding a closure is worse than showing it)
AND FLAGGED 'לבדיקה' (+ GitHub issue), because either this patch is wrong (the point still exists: bring it back,
one line) or the IAA used an old name.
Checked by Eli against the chart, 2026-09-29.
